name: Googie
summary: The roadside style of the American car age. Coffee shops, motels and car washes got upswept roofs, bright signs and space-age shapes to catch a driver at speed.

philosophy.core_thesis: A roadside building must be a sign: it must show a driver at 50 km/h what it sells and why it is new.
design_principles: Lift the roof in a bold slope or a fold so that it reads from the road.
Tie the sign to the building and make it as big as the roof.
Use space-age forms such as boomerangs, starbursts, atoms and saucers.
Fill the front with glass so that the interior is the show.
Cantilever the roof past the walls to give a feeling of flight.
Use bright colour and neon so that the building works at night.
anti_patterns: A plain box with a small sign
Heavy masonry walls with few windows

massing.form: A low pavilion under a large, dynamic roof; the roof and the sign are the main shapes.
massing.proportion: Wide and low, with a tall sign or spire that stands higher than the roof.
massing.roof: Upswept, folded or butterfly roofs of steel, often with a strong tilt of 10 to 30 degrees.
massing.relation_to_ground: The building sits on a slab beside a parking lot, with its glass front open to the road.

structure.system: Light steel frames and thin concrete shells; the roof is a cantilever carried by few slim columns.
structure.span_and_module: A bay of 4 to 6m, with a roof overhang of 2 to 4m.
structure.expression: Slim steel columns, bold rafters and folded plates show the lightness; the stone work is a thin accent.

materials.finish: Smooth and bright; plaster, enamel and chrome, with neon and painted signs for effect.

facade.composition: A glass front under a bold roof edge, with a sign tower or a boomerang pylon at one side.
facade.openings: Large plate-glass walls, often 60% of the front, with thin steel frames.
facade.solid_to_void: Void dominates: glass covers 50–70% of the front.

light_and_space.daylight: Glass lets in strong daylight, and at night the neon and the interior light make the building glow.
light_and_space.spatial_sequence: The driver sees the sign, parks, and enters directly from the car park into an open room.
light_and_space.interior_character: A bright open room with a counter, booths and bold laminate; the ceiling follows the shape of the roof.

ornament.attitude: Ornament is a sign: the shape of the roof and the lettering carry the message.

rules.rule: Make the sign or the roof the focal point.
Set the bright colour against dark night sky.
Slope the roof line toward the road.
Make the sign taller than the roof edge.
Frame the interior with a long glass wall.

emotion.target_response: Excitement and optimism: the viewer feels a roadside rocket that promises a fast, bright future.

avoid_when: The brief asks for quiet, restrained or domestic mid-century living.
The scene is an urban or monumental civic place.

modifiers.how: Lower the roof slope, remove the sign pylon and use timber and brick with a muted palette.

sources.title: Alan Hess, Googie: Fifties Coffee Shop Architecture (Chronicle Books, 1985)
